correctness.rationale: For \(A=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{pmatrix}\), the SIS condition is exactly \(A^2=-I_2\), giving \(a^2+b^2=-1\), \(b(a+c)=0\), and \(b^2+c^2=-1\). Over \(\mathbb F_9=\mathbb F_3(u)\) with \(u^2=-1\), the \(b=0\) branch has four solutions and the \(b\ne0\) branch has six, for exactly ten. Exact exhaustive enumeration independently confirms the count. For each solution, \(G=[I_2\mid A]\) satisfies \(GG^T=0\); exhaustive code enumeration gives six distance-two and four distance-three self-dual codes. The explicit witness has weight enumerator \(1+32z^3+48z^4\).

value.rationale: Table 1 is presented as a computational validation of the paper\'s SIS constructions over small fields, and \(q=9\) is the only displayed square-field row whose count breaks the nearby \(q+1\) pattern. Correcting \(8\) to \(10\) changes the finite classification itself. More importantly for coding theory, the two missing structural branches include four SIS matrices whose systematic codes are MDS \([4,2,3]_9\), so the correction upgrades the attainable code quality shown by that row from only AMDS to include MDS. The exact finite classification and explicit witness are reusable for checking the paper\'s small-field computations.
